title: How the Bangladesh Field Hospital Became the People's Health Centre
conflicts: Hospital site named as Melaghar (TBS), Bisramganj (Daily Star 2023), Agartala (Prothom Alo, Daily Star 2018) or the Tripura border (PHM); story says Agartala, near the border. Passport burned (Chowdhury to Prothom Alo) vs torn up (Daily Star quoting him); story says 'destroyed'. Founding: April 1972 concept paper and conversion 'on the last Sunday of 1972' (TBS) vs simply 1972 elsewhere. Naming: Mujib picked from Chowdhury's list (TBS) vs both proposed three and chose together (Daily Star); story uses the common ground. Savar's distance from Dhaka: about 40 km (Magsaysay) vs 'about 3 kilometres' (PHM, apparently an error); story says 'outside Dhaka'. Field-hospital volunteers: young men and women (Prothom Alo) vs women stressed (PHM, Daily Star); story says 'many of them women'.
notes: Chowdhury's line on access to training rests on one source (Daily Star, Aasha Mehreen Amin). Company field kept to 'Gonoshasthaya Kendra' alone because adding 'Bangladesh Field Hospital' made the repeat screen flag unrelated hospital editions. Quote stance: affirms (Analects VI.28).
